chunks: 4203 - Ibn Muskan narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Qaṣīr, who said:

I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “Indeed, when Ibrāhīm عليه السلام wanted to slaughter the ram, Iblīs came to him and said: ‘This is mine.’ So Ibrāhīm عليه السلام said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘I have such-and-such a share of it.’ Ibrāhīm عليه السلام said: ‘No.’ Then he continued naming one limb after another of the sheep, while Ibrāhīm عليه السلام kept refusing him, until he came to the spleen and named it, so he gave it to him. Thus it is the morsel of Satan.”

And al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: “If meat is together with the spleen on a skewer, the meat is eaten when it is above the spleen. But if it is below the spleen, it is not eaten. Its broth may be eaten, because the spleen is within a membrane and nothing comes down from it unless it is pierced. If it is pierced, what flows from it runs out, and whatever is beneath it of the broth is not eaten. And if a fish whose eating is permissible is placed with a jarrī fish or other than it from what is not permissible to eat on a skewer, the one that has scales is eaten when it is on the skewer above the jarrī and above those which are not eaten. But if it is below the jarrī, it is not eaten.”

key_terms.جُوذَابُهُ: its broth or gravy, referring to what drips or is cooked beneath
key_terms.جِرِّيٍّ: a type of fish not permissible to eat in this context
key_terms.سَفُّودٍ: a skewer used for roasting meat or fish together
key_terms.فُلُوسٌ: scales, the feature marking a fish here as permissible to eat
key_terms.لُقْمَةُ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ: the morsel of Satan, describing the spleen in the narrative
key_terms.ٱلطِّحَالِ: the spleen, identified here as a distinct organ with special legal treatment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about eating meat cooked with spleen or lawful fish cooked with unlawful fish?
ai.summary: This hadith combines a narrative about Ibrāhīm عليه السلام and the spleen being designated as the portion of Satan with legal rulings from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام on food contamination in cooking. It explains that lawful food remains edible when placed above an impure or unlawful item in a skewer arrangement, but not when placed below it if contamination can descend.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4203 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Abdul Rahim Al-Qasir, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), say:
"Indeed, when Ibrahim (as), peace be upon him, intended to slaughter the ram, Iblis came to him and said: 'This belongs to me.'
Ibrahim (as), peace be upon him, replied: 'No.'
Iblis said: 'I have a share in it,'
Ibrahim (as), peace be upon him, responded: 'No.'
Iblis then began naming each part of the sheep, but Ibrahim (as), peace be upon him, rejected him until he finally mentioned the spleen (al-tihal).
At that point, Ibrahim (as), peace be upon him, gave it to him. Therefore, it is considered the morsel of Satan."

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"If meat is placed with the spleen on a skewer, the meat may be eaten if it is placed above the spleen.
However, if it is placed below the spleen, it should not be eaten. Its dripping (fat and juices) may be consumed because the spleen is enclosed in a membrane, and nothing comes out of it unless it is punctured. If it is punctured, its contents will leak out, and the dripping below it should not be consumed.
If a permissible fish is placed on a skewer with a catfish or any other fish that is not permissible to eat, the fish with scales may be eaten if it is placed above the catfish or the non-permissible fish on the skewer. However, if it is placed below the catfish, it should not be eaten."
